completion_conditions: A ledger the loop writes after its last delivery point is carried by the next branch-state sync.
A file that was already delivered is never carried twice, and the carry is idempotent.
The carry never picks up a file belonging to another task's contract or any non-ledger mirror record it was not asked to deliver.
The full suite, the goal-loop suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: MEASURED. After each goal completed, the coordinator checkout held ledger files absent from main — e.g. `L-20260805T073358816023Z-baf26752` (type `mergegate`, 'Goal loop merged PR #289 ...') and `L-20260805T073400360295Z-ec8cb045` (type `check`, 'Goal loop marked T-... done: PR already merged'). `git merge origin/main` then aborted with 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge', and continuing required backing the files up and deleting them by hand. That happened on 2026-08-05 (twice), and again on 2026-08-06 (twice).

MECHANISM, read from source. `_sync_state_to_branch` (`scripts/shiki_loop.py:1000`) is the ONLY delivery path, and it is called from exactly three effectors: `:1850` (create_pr), `:1890` (dispatch_repair), `:1954` (rerun_cca). The `merge` and `mark_done` effectors (`:2011-2013`) append ledgers and never sync. By then the task branch is merged, so there is nothing left to sync to.

SCOPE OF THE HARM, stated honestly. No dangling reference reaches main: the task file on main references only the entries that were delivered, so `validate_shiki` and MergeGate stay green, and GitHub — source of truth #1 — records the merge itself durably. What is lost is the mirror's record of the loop's own final actions, and what is PAID is a manual conflict resolution on every subsequent sync. This is a mirror-completeness and operability defect, not an evidence-integrity one, and the contract should not overstate it.

REJECTED — reordering the closeout so the entries can ride it. `docs/adr/0012` pins the closeout decision table, and the closeout merge record cannot exist before the closeout is merged. Reordering is a governance change for a bookkeeping problem.

CHOSEN — a self-healing carry. Record post-closeout bookkeeping as undelivered, and have the next branch-state sync — for any task, in any goal — carry every undelivered loop-authored ledger file. That matches what the manual 'carry ... ledger evidence onto the task branch' commits already in this repository's history do by hand, needs no reordering and no ADR change. The lag is bounded and self-clearing; the final entries of the final goal remain undelivered until the next goal runs, which must be stated rather than hidden.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-06). MUST-CHANGE: `scripts/shiki_loop.py`; `tests/test_dispatch_state_sync.py` (7 references — owns the sync property); `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py` (12 references — the heaviest driver, imports the sync internals directly).

TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS THAT KEEP THE LOCK SET AT THREE, both measured. (a) Implement the carry inside `_sync_state_to_branch`, NOT inside `_evidence_relatives_for_task`: `tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py` calls that function directly at `:320`, `:336`, `:498` and asserts on its output, so changing what it returns would pull that file in. (b) Do not change `_sync_state_to_branch`'s signature: `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py:209-224` monkeypatches it.

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks): `tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py`, `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py`, `tests/test_loop_lock_guard.py` (prose reference only), and `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` which drives the loop end to end. `scripts/shiki_tasks.py:39` and `scripts/mergegate_check.py:190` mention the sync in COMMENTS describing what rides a branch; they are not code references and must not be edited.

Risk is medium and honest: this changes which files a state sync commits, not what any gate enforces, and no approval source, schema or workflow moves. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither PR triggers the Guardian gate.

tasks.scope:
In `scripts/shiki_loop.py`, stop stranding the ledger entries the loop writes after its last delivery point.

MECHANISM, read from source: `_sync_state_to_branch` (`:1000`) is the ONLY delivery path and is called from exactly three effectors — `:1850` create_pr, `:1890` dispatch_repair, `:1954` rerun_cca. The `merge` and `mark_done` effectors (`:2011-2013`) append ledgers and never sync, and by then the task branch is merged so there is nothing to sync to.

Make the loop record such an entry as UNDELIVERED when it is written, and make `_sync_state_to_branch` — on its next run, for ANY task in ANY goal — carry every undelivered loop-authored ledger file onto that branch and clear the marker. The carry must be idempotent: a file already on the branch is not carried again, and a second sync produces no second diff. It must carry ONLY loop-authored ledger files that were never delivered — never another task's contract records, and never any other mirror record it was not asked to deliver.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT KEEP THIS INSIDE THREE FILES, both measured:
  (a) Implement the carry INSIDE `_sync_state_to_branch`, not inside `_evidence_relatives_for_task`. `tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py` calls that function directly at `:320`, `:336` and `:498` and asserts on its output; changing what it returns pulls that file into the locks.
  (b) Do NOT change `_sync_state_to_branch`'s signature — `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py:209-224` monkeypatches it.

State the residual lag in a comment rather than hiding it: the final entries of the final goal stay undelivered until some later goal runs a sync. That is bounded and self-clearing, and it is the honest cost of not reordering the closeout.

TESTS. `tests/test_dispatch_state_sync.py` owns the sync property: add that an undelivered entry is carried on the next sync, that the carry is idempotent over two syncs, that an already-delivered file is not carried again, and that nothing outside the loop-authored undelivered set is ever carried. `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py` drives the internals against a real repository: add a regression that reproduces the measured sequence — a merged closeout leaves an entry undelivered, the next task's sync carries it, and the coordinator checkout no longer diverges from the branch.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: after a goal completes, `git merge origin/main` in the coordinator checkout aborts with 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge', naming ledger files the loop wrote. Continuing requires backing them up and deleting them by hand.
  Measured four times on 2026-08-05/06. Examples: `L-20260805T073358816023Z-baf26752` (type `mergegate`, 'Goal loop merged PR #289 ...') and `L-20260805T073400360295Z-ec8cb045` (type `check`, 'Goal loop marked T-... done: PR already merged'), both present in the coordinator checkout and absent from main.
  Honest scope: no dangling reference reaches main — the task file there references only the delivered entries, so `validate_shiki` and MergeGate stay green and GitHub records the merge durably. What is lost is the mirror's record of the loop's own final actions; what is paid is a manual conflict resolution on every later sync.
  Why not reorder the closeout: `docs/adr/0012` pins its decision table, and a closeout's merge record cannot exist before the closeout is merged.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: mark post-delivery ledgers undelivered and carry them on the next sync — which is what the manual 'carry ... ledger evidence onto the task branch' commits already in this repository's history do by hand.
  Reproducible when: the measured sequence leaves no untracked ledger file in the coordinator checkout after the next task's sync, and a second sync produces no diff.
